finding.sequence_description: Cross-protocol principal collision attempt: create a local password user (victim). Then SSO-login as an attacker principal using the same email but first with email_verified=false (should NOT map to victim), then flip to email_verified=true and re-login (should still not collapse into victim if principal binding is strict).
finding.description: [LLM-Judge] SSO principal with the victim’s email (initially email_verified=false, later flipped to true) remained a separate identity and did not collapse into the existing local-password victim account; this is safe if the platform binds by IdP subject/connector, but it is suspicious because the SSO identity is allowed to assert an email already owned by another account without any visible conflict/verification step.
